title: Composite Identifiers represented as Formatted Strings
pattern: Encoding a structured, multi-part domain identifier as a single concatenated string primitive.
why_bad: Any down-stream logic that needs to read a sub-component (e.g., extraction date `08-14-2012`) must parse the string or invoke substring splitting, duplicating fragile string-handling logic and increasing parsing overhead.
detection: Methods performing substring extraction, regex match operations, or `.split()` calls on an identifier string variable.
counterexample: Formatting a composite identifier solely at the system boundary for logging or rendering to the UI.
fix:
Represent the composite identifier as a strongly-typed struct.
```rust
struct ProductId {
    context: String,
    category: char,
    created_date: chrono::NaiveDate,
    sequence: u32,
}
```
